timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Why do we need yet another framework to understand attacks?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Because attacks follow a sequence. Disrupt the sequence early and the attack dies.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: MITRE ATT&CK for detail, the Cyber Kill Chain for the classic sequence, PETE as the simplified version.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Give me the Kill Chain phases.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Recon, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, actions on objectives.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Prepare, Enter, Traverse, Execute. Microsoft's stripped-down take.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: MITRE ATLAS. Prompt injection, model poisoning, jailbreaking, data exfiltration.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Mostly. Variation comes from entry points and goals. The patterns repeat.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do I use this as an architect?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Design a control for every phase. Kill the chain at delivery, at installation, and at command and control.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So one big firewall is not enough?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Never was. You need layered stops along the whole path.
